title: Odysseus: The Beggar in His Own Hall
subtitle: Disguised homecoming, a bow only he can string, and a bed that cannot move

learningObjectives.text: Why does Odysseus return disguised as a beggar?

main.author: Homer
main.locator: Book 23, Odysseus explains the rooted bed; local text file lines 10218-10223 (physical file lines, not ancient verse numbers)
main.excerpt: There was a young olive growing within the precincts of the house, in full vigour, and about as thick as a bearing-post. I built my room round this with strong walls of stone and a roof to cover them, and I made the doors strong and well-fitting. Then I cut off the top boughs of the olive tree and left the stump standing.
main.note: Verbatim local text with whitespace normalized. Lesson analysis is interpretation, not part of this quotation.

narrativeBlocks.title: Alone, on a foreign ship
narrativeBlocks.body: Twenty years after leaving, Odysseus reaches Ithaca — as the prophecy said, alone and on another man's ship. Athena wrinkles him into an old beggar: the suiters would kill a stranger outright; a beggar can walk his own hall and take its measure.

narrativeBlocks.title: Insults at his own table
narrativeBlocks.body: The beggar begs from the suitors in his palace, takes their mockery and their thrown footstool, and memorises every insult. His old dog Argos, dying on the dungheap, wags his tail once and dies — the only one who knows him.

narrativeBlocks.title: The bow contest
narrativeBlocks.body: Penelope announces she will marry whoever strings Odysseus's great bow and shoots through twelve axe-heads. Every suitor fails. The beggar asks to try — they laugh — strings it effortlessly, and sends an arrow through all twelve.

narrativeBlocks.title: The reckoning
narrativeBlocks.body: The beggar drops the disguise and the hall becomes an archery range: every suitor dies. Twenty years of patience, disguises, and restraint end in one afternoon — the slow story finally cashes its cheques.

narrativeBlocks.title: The immovable bed
narrativeBlocks.body: Penelope tests the stranger: she orders his bed moved outside. Odysseus explodes — the bed is built around a living olive tree; it cannot move unless a man has cut it. Only her husband could know that. The test is passed — the epic's last recognition is the quietest and the best.

quiz.prompt: Why does Athena disguise Odysseus as a beggar?

choices.text: The suiters would kill a stranger — as a beggar he can enter his own hall unseen and judge them
He lost his memory on the voyage
The disguise is punishment from Poseidon

quiz.explanation: Disguise lets him assess the enemy in his own house before striking — Odysseus's signature patience.

quiz.prompt: How does Penelope finally confirm it is Odysseus?

choices.text: She asks for his bed to be moved — his fury reveals it is rooted to a living olive tree, a secret only he could know
She recognizes a scar on his leg
He produces the ring from their wedding

quiz.explanation: The bed built around a rooted olive tree is a secret only the real Odysseus could know — the epic's most intimate recognition.
